question: Uppercase 'MAY NOT' is not defined by RFC 2119, yet RFC 8174 makes uppercase the trigger for RFC 2119 semantics. Which currently-in-force RFCs use it, and what does each occurrence mean?
corpus: rsync rsync.rfc-editor.org::rfcs-text-only, retrieved 2026-09-07 (9828 rfcNNNN.txt); RFC status from rfc-index.xml the same day
selection: RFCs whose text contains uppercase 'MAY NOT', that are NOT obsoleted, and that cite RFC 2119 or RFC 8174
classification_is_a_reading: Every one of these was read in context by hand. The categories are my reading of intent, not a fact about the documents. 'unresolved' means I could not decide, which is itself the finding: an implementer cannot decide either.

category_key.boilerplate: the RFC's own conventions section lists "MAY NOT" as an RFC 2119 key word. RFC 2119 defines no such term.
category_key.permission: reads as 'need not' / is permitted to omit
category_key.idiom: the fixed phrase 'MAY or MAY NOT', meaning optional either way
category_key.quoted: quotes or tabulates another RFC's usage
category_key.unresolved: I read it and could not tell which was meant

occurrences.note: Vendor Private Extension MAY NOT appear more than once in an SCSP packet
'This string MAY NOT be NULL terminated' - prohibition on the sender or a warning to the parser; the difference is what a receiver must tolerate
SMON MIB: objects that MAY NOT be modified while the control row is active, entries that MAY NOT exist in the active state, a dataSource that MAY NOT be referenced
'MAY NOT necessarily reside in the 6Bone registry'
'All ports MAY NOT transmit the same number of frames if their Iload is not the same'
hosts MAY NOT use unassigned addresses / tuples; host and gateway MAY NOT switch transport protocol
conventions section lists "MAY NOT" among the key words 'to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119]'
'Multiple errors MAY NOT be reported in the same ERROR_RESPONSE'
'MAY or MAY NOT specify the remote port(s)'
'the secret ... MAY NOT be configured' (i.e. might not be)
'integers that MAY or MAY NOT be included in the tuple'
'MAY NOT be a requirement'; 'it MAY NOT be reasonable to expect'
'a server ... MAY NOT be able to determine whether a mailbox has children'
'MAY or MAY NOT include a revocation support extension'
'the secret ... MAY NOT be configured' (same sentence as RFC3162)
'A private extension MAY or MAY NOT be included in the capabilities list'
'It MAY NOT advertise the IHAVE capability' in a bullet list whose neighbours are MUST and MUST NOT
'it MAY NOT start preserving that data', paired with 'it MAY stop preserving' - the parallel argues permission, the neighbouring MUST NOT argues prohibition
'MAY or MAY NOT require the inter-AS TE tunnel ending addresses to be known'
discretionary attributes 'MAY or MAY NOT be sent in a particular UPDATE message'
S9.1.1 'the route MAY NOT serve as an input to the next phase of route selection' - errata 5000 corrects this to MUST NOT; Held for Document Update since 2017-04-19
the BGP-4 implementation report tabulates RFC 4271's usage and records the requirement level of two features literally as 'RFC2119: MAY NOT' and 'RFC2119: MAY or MAY NOT'
terminology section lists "MAY NOT" among the key words 'to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119'
'MAY NOT be suitable for use with applications that perform dot-segment normalization'
'Namespace Authorities MAY or MAY NOT choose to disclose service mechanisms'
'Clients MAY or MAY NOT include the RDN attribute(s) in this list'
conventions section lists "MAY NOT" among the key words 'to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119'
'some implementations MAY NOT be capable of fully utilizing the extensions'
"The 'failed' disposition type MAY NOT be used for the situation in which ..."
WebDAV: a resource 'MAY NOT have values for properties like DAV:getcontentlanguage'
'The MAGIC option MAY NOT be implemented, as it has been deprecated'
'specifies in which PANA messages they MAY or MAY NOT be present'
'calculation however MAY NOT be performed while fax is in progress' - forbidden, or cannot be
'Future versions of SLAPP MAY NOT mandate support for earlier major versions'
Diameter AVP occurrence tables: 'specify in which Diameter messages they MAY or MAY NOT be present'
'a TinyIPFIX Template that has been sent once MAY NOT be withdrawn and MUST NOT expire'
'A single packet MAY NOT contain data from more than one Parse Info Header or Data Unit', next sentence uses MUST NOT for the converse
'An implementation MAY NOT place an ELI/EL after a regular Adj-SID' / 'MAY NOT insert an ELI/EL'
'it MAY NOT emit CBOR preferred serializations' (published 2025)
